context: Treat this as an evidence-integrity incident, not a cleanup task. First inventory precisely what survives in committed derived data versus what is permanently lost, so the packets can state an honest verification status instead of implying reproducibility they no longer have. Then fix the durability defect at the source so no future generation depends on a purgeable path, preferring committed normalized responses (they are small) or a checksummed backup manifest outside /tmp. Only then decide, with Joe, whether restoring an auditable chain justifies re-running a generation.
description: Verified 2026-08-03 on main at 0661311. The runner wrote every raw and normalized response only under /tmp/memory-behavioral-vN-raw, and each committed result record pins an absolute /tmp path plus a response_sha256 that the scorer and auditor re-read on every invocation. macOS purged /tmp after the 2026-07-29 runs, so all three generations of raw evidence are gone (v3 144 runs, v4 45 runs, v5 180 runs). Only v2-era backups survive under ~/Developer/memory-governance-artifacts. Consequences reproduced directly: score now raises FileNotFoundError on the first record, and audit reports raw response unavailable for every run, so no committed packet can be revalidated and the recorded report SHAs can never be re-derived. Committed derived data retains decision labels, metric components, safety flags, and extra authority or verification, but NOT answer text, dispositions, authority lists, or verification_status.

work_units.evidence: commit 12abc48. New evidence.py resolver plus schema 6 records that embed the normalized response, so future generations verify with no external directory; raw root default moved off /tmp to a durable state dir with env override. Proven: all 72 committed v2 records now resolve via archive fallback and verify their recorded sha256 with zero record edits. Resolution is asymmetric by design - mismatch at the recorded path raises (corruption), mismatch on an archive guess continues the search because run ids repeat across generations (caught a real cross-generation collision during implementation). score now reports unresolvable runs and adds a gate blocker instead of raising FileNotFoundError. 63 scorer tests pass incl. 9 new evidence tests
